text: AI agents now hold wallets, and move real money. A spending limit stops an agent spending too much. It doesn't stop it paying the wrong person. Paying the same invoice twice. Or paying a fake one.
So what if every payment had to prove itself, before a single cent moved?
Scalehouse is live on Arc mainnet. The home page shows real payments, read straight from the chain, and walks you through exactly what every payment goes through.
Start by opening a house. That's your business. Connect your wallet, give it a name, and set how much can go out on its own, per payment and per day. Approve once, and your house is open.

To pay someone, paste their wallet, the amount, and what it's for. Tap pay. The agent screens the wallet against Circle's USDC blocklist, checks your budget, and pays through its Circle wallet. About thirty seconds later. Paid.
Tap open receipt. Every payment gets a receipt anyone can check. Who was paid, how much, and what for. The agent's own reasoning, hashed on chain. And every step, replayed from the contract.

Want a person to check bigger payments? Add a confirmer by name. They get a private link, with no wallet needed. A payment over your limit waits. Your confirmer opens the link, checks it, and taps confirm.

Why it can't go wrong. The wallet is locked the moment a payment is recorded. A second check confirms it. Then the contract on Arc works out the amount itself, and pays the locked wallet. Once. The agent never holds a key.

Don't take our word for it. On the attack lab, anyone can attack the agent, for real. Paste your wallet, and the agent pays you. Hide an instruction in an invoice. The agent ignores it. Hijack the agent outright. The contract freezes the payment. Six attacks. All stopped.
And it's already moving real money. Three people, paid on mainnet, each in under thirty seconds. Here's what they said.
Why Scalehouse? It's as fast as a wallet send. It can't pay the wrong person, or pay twice. And it's built on Circle and Arc, end to end.
Scalehouse. Weighed in public. Paid once.
